claims.claim: Zhang et al.'s creative-writing benchmarks were poem continuation, story generation and joke writing.
claims.source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning and Shi (Northeastern/Stanford/WVU), arXiv 2510.01171 v4
claims.quote: poem continuation, story generation, and joke writing

claims.claim: In Zhang et al.'s poem task the mean semantic diversity score rose from 11.4 under direct prompting to 21.9 under VS-Standard and 25.8 under VS-CoT.
claims.source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning and Shi (Northeastern/Stanford/WVU), arXiv 2510.01171 v4

claims.claim: In Zhang et al.'s human study of 90 annotators, poem diversity was rated 2.39 for VS-Standard against 1.90 for direct prompting on a four-point scale.
claims.source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning and Shi (Northeastern/Stanford/WVU), arXiv 2510.01171 v4

claims.claim: Zhang et al. observe an emergent trend in which larger models benefit more from Verbalized Sampling.
claims.source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning and Shi (Northeastern/Stanford/WVU), arXiv 2510.01171 v4
claims.quote: larger models benefit more from VS

claims.claim: Lanchantin et al. argue that shifting all probability onto one of several equally rewarded generations is an optimal solution to the reinforcement-learning objective.
claims.source: Lanchantin, Chen, Dhuliawala, Yu, Weston, Sukhbaatar and Kulikov (Meta), arXiv 2501.18101 v4
claims.quote: shifting all probability to only one of them is an optimal solution

claims.claim: Lanchantin et al. report that adjusting the sampling temperature did not alleviate the persona-diversity problem and brought a sharp decline in quality.
claims.source: Lanchantin, Chen, Dhuliawala, Yu, Weston, Sukhbaatar and Kulikov (Meta), arXiv 2501.18101 v4
claims.quote: not alleviate this problem, as we see a sharp decline in quality

claims.claim: Lanchantin et al. measured Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct generating the persona name Astrid more than ten per cent of the time.
claims.source: Lanchantin, Chen, Dhuliawala, Yu, Weston, Sukhbaatar and Kulikov (Meta), arXiv 2501.18101 v4
claims.quote: generates the name “Astrid” more than 10% of the time

claims.claim: Lanchantin et al. report DivPO training was 74.6% more diverse than DPO on story generation with a 6.4% drop in quality.
claims.source: Lanchantin, Chen, Dhuliawala, Yu, Weston, Sukhbaatar and Kulikov (Meta), arXiv 2501.18101 v4
claims.quote: DivPO with ρ = 0.3 is 74.6% more diverse

claims.claim: Lanchantin et al. found that GPT-4o failed to produce diverse personas.
claims.source: Lanchantin, Chen, Dhuliawala, Yu, Weston, Sukhbaatar and Kulikov (Meta), arXiv 2501.18101 v4

claims.claim: Sharma et al. measured that AI assistants' free-form feedback on a text passage does not depend solely on the passage's content but shifts with the user's stated preference.
claims.source: Sharma, Tong, Korbak, Duvenaud, Askell et al. (Anthropic), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: assistants does not depend solely on the content of the text
claims.page: Section 3.1, AI Assistants Can Give Biased Feedback

claims.claim: Sharma et al. measured Claude 1.3 wrongly admitting mistakes on 98% of questions when challenged by the user.
claims.source: Sharma, Tong, Korbak, Duvenaud, Askell et al. (Anthropic), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: wrongly admits mistakes on 98% of questions
claims.page: Section 3.2, AI Assistants Can Be Easily Swayed

claims.claim: Sharma et al. found that matching a user's views is one of the most predictive features of human preference judgments in the hh-rlhf data.
claims.source: Sharma, Tong, Korbak, Duvenaud, Askell et al. (Anthropic), ICLR 2024
claims.quote: matching a user’s views is one of the most predictive features

claims.claim: Sharma et al. constructed a less sycophantic preference model by prompting the Claude 2 preference model with a dialog asking for truthful responses.
claims.source: Sharma, Tong, Korbak, Duvenaud, Askell et al. (Anthropic), ICLR 2024

claims.claim: Shumailov et al. report that indiscriminate use of model-generated content in training causes irreversible defects in the resulting models.
claims.source: Shumailov, Shumaylov, Zhao, Papernot, Anderson and Gal, Nature 631:755-759 (2024)
claims.quote: causes irreversible defects in the resulting models

claims.claim: Shumailov et al. found that enforcing a repetition penalty of 2.0 caused the language models' perplexity to double compared with the original.
claims.source: Shumailov, Shumaylov, Zhao, Papernot, Anderson and Gal, Nature 631:755-759 (2024)
claims.quote: enforcing this for the LLM experiments causes the perplexity to double
